## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0db54351e8e6ed14e0b367b9663eeb8774e6deaa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json + none
Security-touching: yes

PR #36568 (card #36541), net diff against merge-base `d463c46f`: 4 files, +44 / -12 (the three `hits` files and one changeset). No implementing file is in the diff; the protocol it teaches (PR #36517, `45ef94ef`) was read on `main` at `3b589215`, never reviewed. Check-runs on the head: 44 total, 28 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending (among them Lint and Repo Gates, Lint docs and code guards, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. The diff carries no schema, validator, gate or runtime file; no input that was accepted is refused and none that was refused is accepted. Right.
- Public surface: the published `@objectstack/skills` bundle gains one paragraph in `objectstack-data` § Object Extension Model, loses five restatements in the same always-loaded file, gains eval case 27, and has case 26's reference answer edited in one parenthesis. Right as a surface change; one sentence of the new paragraph is wrong at its edge (S1 below).
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. The protocol was added by PR #36517; this PR teaches it.
- Token ratchet: ceiling row not raised (the file is paid for by same-file cuts); the gate's verdict is the green lint lanes on this head. Right.
- Security-touching reads `yes`, and it is meant, on the letter of the arm's rule and for one hunk only: the hunk at SKILL.md line 71 edits the heading of the `sharingModel` (org-wide default record visibility) table and removes the words "(ADR-0090 D4; legacy aliases removed)" from the always-loaded file. That hunk sits in sharing teaching and takes a sharing statement out of the entry file (it stays in `references/lint-rules.md`, `security-owd-alias`). The new arrangement paragraph, `{ list, hidden: true }` and both eval cases are presentation only and teach no permission, sharing or credential behaviour; had the PR been those hunks alone the line would read `no`. The adopting seat decides the `security` label on that basis.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36541-skills-custom-arrangement.md`: `@objectstack/skills` patch. Matches what the diff publishes (skill prose and an eval fixture, no accept-set change, no API). Check Changeset is green on the head.

Clause-②: no — agreed. Nothing in the diff narrows what the platform accepts; the PR body and the changeset both carry the line and they agree.

The changeset is not under ④, but its first bullet repeats the sentence S1 names ("In any other package both keys are refused ..."); the fix of S1 should carry the same wording there.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in report 7087735893. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, `evals/README.md` outside the claimed surface: answered by claim amendment 7087768569; the clause is one index line for case 27 and is accurate. Accepted.
- Deviation, case 26's reference answer edited: required, the old parenthesis ("an extension has neither key") is false on `main` since `45ef94ef`. Prompt and assertions unchanged. Accepted.
- Deviation, ceiling row left at 6710 with the file below it: accepted; lowering it edits the ratchet script, outside this card.
- Deviation, `git fetch --deepen` moved the shared `origin/main` ref, and several gates were read locally on a partial build: no effect on the head; the check-runs are the verdicts.
- Overlap with draft #36158 in `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: ruled by the seat for #36527 (whichever lands second replays its text). Not a finding here; the replay must keep the S1 wording once fixed.
- PR body acceptance note 4 says the paragraph leaves "a `.custom` package that is not the object's pair is not refused, it is skipped" to the refusal texts and the docs page. The paragraph does not merely leave it out; it states the opposite. See S1.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no code, no query, no id materialisation in the diff. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

**skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md** — the new paragraph, sentence by sentence against `main`:

- "Only the pair's extension may also write `fieldGroups` and `relatedLists`, shaped as on an object." Holds. `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldGroups` is an array of the object's group schema and `relatedLists` the object's entry plus `hidden` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_WRITER` and the two key descriptions); the fold serves only the object's own pairs (`applyCustomArrangement`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts`, `pairs.includes(packageId)`). A per-package pair of an earlier version, served second, is still "a pair"; the sentence is not false for it.
- "A written key replaces that arrangement whole (the owner's and every `place`)". Holds: the fold applies the key last, after `applyExtensionPlacements`, and merges nothing entry by entry.
- "an unlisted field shows after the last group". Holds (the trailing bucket; a field of the owner or another extension loses a `group` the arrangement replaced).
- "an unnamed tab still shows after the listed ones". Holds for both kinds the brief asks about, on the word "still": a tab the owner's declared list showed and the arrangement does not name is carried (`carried`, placed after the listed entries); a list the owner hid by leaving it out was never a tab, is not carried, and stays hidden (`unlisted: 'hidden'`, `deriveRelatedLists.ts` lines 603 to 607) until the arrangement names it. The sentence does not promise that list reappears. See N2 for what it leaves unsaid.
- "`{ list: 'crm_note', hidden: true }` hides a tab". Holds (`hidden` on the extension entry only; `relatedListEntryHidden` in the fold; the served `_relatedListsArrangement.hidden`).
- "In any other package both keys are refused at those doors: use `place`." Wrong at its edge, S1.
- The doors ("those doors" is save, publish and install, `os validate` / `os build`, from the sentence before): each read at its call site on `main`: save `protocol-save.ts:1390`, publish `protocol-history-and-publish.ts:1062`, both through `objectExtensionItemRefusal` (`protocol-object-extension-item.ts:257`); `validate.ts:895`; `compile.ts:948`; install `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3192`. Holds for a writer that is not a `.custom` package.
- The field-hide recipe (a group whose `visibleWhen` is false) is not taught by this paragraph, so its two limits are not owed here.

S1 (should-fix) — SKILL.md line 390, "In any other package both keys are refused at those doors" is false for a `.custom` package that is not the object's pair. On `main` the one judge refuses only a writer for which `isCustomizationPackage` is false (`judgeExtensionArrangement`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-arrangement.ts:91` to `:94`: "In a `.custom` package nothing is refused"), and the schema's own description says so in terms: "A `.custom` package that is not this object's pair is not refused at those doors: the registry merge does not apply what it writes here ... and the boot log names it" (`CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_WRITER`, `object.zod.ts`). In the skill's vocabulary "the pair" is the base's paired `.custom` package (`hotcrm.custom`), so "any other package" includes another App's `.custom`. The skill therefore teaches an author that a green `os validate` / save / install proves the arrangement sits in the right package, when for that writer every door is green and the fold drops the key with one boot-log line. The neighbouring `__c` sentence on `main` uses the same phrase over the same predicate; it is outside this diff and was not judged here (what the registry does with another `.custom` package's `__c` field was not read). The new sentence is judged on its own: it hides a silent no-op. The fix does not need to teach the skip, only stop denying it: name the refused writer by what the judge tests, for example "Outside a `.custom` package both keys are refused at those doors: use `place`." (a few bytes over the remaining headroom, to be paid in the same file), and mirror it in the changeset bullet. Eval cases 26 and 27 already say it correctly ("`acme_contracts` is not a `.custom` package, so both keys are refused there") and need no change.

The five payment hunks, each against its surviving home at the head:

- Insert-null note (§ Validation Patterns): `rules/validation.md` lines 80 to 83 carry the same note; "On update, the prior record supplies it" survives as the `script` row's "Merged record — prior row plus this write" (line 17). It leaves the always-loaded file; a grep of the changed eval file found no case leaning on it (the bundle's other eval file was not read). Kept.
- "`unique` defaults to `false`; omit it ...": `rules/indexing.md` line 11. Kept.
- "append-only objects must declare one": same file, the `lifecycle` property row (line 104, "Required for append-only, high-write-rate objects"), and `rules/lifecycle.md` lines 14 to 15. Kept.
- "(ADR-0090 D4; legacy aliases removed)": `references/lint-rules.md` line 23 (`security-owd-alias`, error); the heading still says "the four canonical values" and the Required table "one of the four below". Kept; this is the hunk the Security-touching line answers for.
- `(e.g., "Accounts")`: the object JSON example, line 58. Kept.

**skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json**

- Case 27, reference answer against `main`: the fold over the prompt's owner list `['crm_contact', 'crm_opportunity', 'crm_lead', 'sys_activity']` and the arrangement `['crm_opportunity', 'crm_contact', { list: 'crm_lead', hidden: true }]` serves opportunity, contact, then the carried `sys_activity`, with `crm_lead` hidden for every reader. The answer says exactly that ("the activity stream here"), says `fieldGroups` not written keeps the groups, names the five doors, and states the non-`.custom` boundary correctly. True sentence by sentence.
- Case 27 under the literal grader (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`, case-sensitive substring): all six `must_contain` tokens are in the reference answer; neither forbidden string is ("takes no `overrides` declaration" has a backtick, not a colon, after the word; `name: 'crm_account'` does not occur). Passes its own assertions, read by eye; the dev's 27/27 is consistent.
- Case 27 prompt: the asked behaviour is observable through `hotcrm.custom`, `defineObjectExtension` and `extend: 'crm_account'`, which the prompt does not hand over. `relatedLists` and `hidden: true` are quoted in the prompt (disclosed in the PR body); see N1 for `place`.
- Case 26: the one changed parenthesis ("only the object extension of HotCRM's paired `hotcrm.custom` package writes those keys; here they are refused") is true for `acme_contracts`; the edited answer still carries all five `must_contain` tokens and neither forbidden string.
- Forbidden strings `name: 'crm_account'` and `overrides:` are those case 26 already carries on `main`; a correct answer has no need of either. No correct answer is caught.

N1 (nit) — case 27's `must_contain` token `place` is a substring of "replaces", so an answer that says the key "replaces the tab list" and never names `place` for the add-on package still satisfies it; the "what may `acme_contracts` write instead" half is then not observed by the grader. Case 26 uses `place:`, which the case 27 reference answer also contains. Left as a follow-up; it changes no teaching.

N2 (nit) — "an unnamed tab still shows after the listed ones" leaves two things to the key description: a list the owner hid by leaving it out stays hidden until the arrangement names it, and carried tabs go before a trailing approvals / activity run of the listed ones. Neither is stated falsely. If S1's fix leaves bytes, the first is the one worth a clause.

**skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md** — one clause, "the `.custom` pair's whole arrangement (`relatedLists`, `{ list, hidden: true }`)", matches case 27. Holds.

Attempts to break the design that did not land: a `hidden` entry on a built-in tab (not what the paragraph's example names); the reference extension beside a `place` entry (it carries none); the pair unresolved because the object has no package (the fold names it, the skill's "installed package" framing excludes it); an earlier-version per-package pair (served second, still a pair).

S1 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix; N1 and N2 do not hold the round.

Delta round 1 over record 7087999230 (head `0db54351e8e6ed14e0b367b9663eeb8774e6deaa`, PASS with S1 open). PR #36568, card #36541. The rework is one commit, `90a673de` on parent `0db54351`, no merge of `main` in the hop (merge-base with `origin/main` is still `d463c46f`). It changes 3 files, 3 lines: the last sentence of the new paragraph in `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`, the same sentence in the changeset's first bullet, and one `must_contain` token of eval case 27. `evals/README.md` did not move in the rework. Net diff against the merge-base: 4 files, +44 / -12 (the three `hits` files and the changeset); no implementing file is in the diff. The code the paragraph teaches was read on `origin/main` at `047e1dca`, never reviewed; none of the files read there (the judge, the CLI door, `object.zod.ts`, `customization-package.ts`, the item gate, the install door, the registry fold, the grader) and nothing under `skills/objectstack-data` differs between `d463c46f` and `047e1dca`.

Check-runs on this head: 48 total, 30 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Success includes Lint and Repo Gates, Lint docs and code guards, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint ESLint, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Test Core (1/10, 2/10 and the rollup), Check Changeset (both runs), PR-body guards (both runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard. The lane's "30 green, 0 red" is confirmed.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged by the rework and by the net diff. No schema, validator, gate or runtime file is in the diff. Right.
- Public surface: the published `@objectstack/skills` bundle. The rework narrows one taught sentence from "any other package" to "outside a `.custom` package", so the skill no longer states a refusal the doors do not make. Right.
- Eval surface: case 27's sixth `must_contain` token is `place:` instead of `place`. The assertion set gets stricter (an answer naming `place` only as part of another word, or only in prose, no longer passes); the prompt and the reference answer are unchanged. Right; see N1 below.

- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, unchanged from the earlier record.
- Security-touching stays `yes`, for the reason record 7087999230 gave and for nothing in the rework: the net diff this head carries still holds the hunk at the `sharingModel` table heading (it removes "(ADR-0090 D4; legacy aliases removed)" from the always-loaded file; the statement stays in `references/lint-rules.md`). The three reworked lines teach no permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The adopting seat decides the `security` label on that basis.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36541-skills-custom-arrangement.md`: `@objectstack/skills` patch, unchanged level; it matches what the diff publishes. Check Changeset is green on this head.

Clause-②: no — agreed. Nothing in the diff narrows what the platform accepts; PR body and changeset both carry the line.

The changeset's first bullet now reads "Outside a `.custom` package both keys are refused at save, publish and install and by `os validate` / `os build`, with the prescription to use `place`", the same claim as the skill sentence, as record 7087999230 asked.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both dev reports (7087735893, 7088256111). Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, N2 not done for lack of bytes: accepted, see N2 below.
- Deviation, door suites not re-run in the fix round: no effect; the rework touches no file they read, and the check-runs on this head are the verdicts.
- Deviation, PR body trailer order: outside the reviewed faces; PR-body guards are green on this head.
- PR body acceptance note 4 now agrees with the paragraph: the paragraph no longer says a non-pair `.custom` package is refused; it does not teach the skip, and leaves that to the key descriptions and the docs page. Consistent.
- Overlap with draft #36158 in `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: ruled by the seat (whichever lands second replays its text). The replay must keep the "Outside a `.custom` package" wording.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no code, no query, no id materialisation in the diff. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

**skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md** — the reworked sentence, line 390 at this head: "Outside a `.custom` package both keys are refused at those doors: use `place`." ("those doors" are the previous sentence's: save, publish and install, `os validate` / `os build`.)

Against `main`:

- The one judge, `judgeExtensionArrangement` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-arrangement.ts:91` to `:109`), returns a refusal for every arrangement key of every `objectExtensions` entry whenever the package id is a non-empty string for which `isCustomizationPackage` is false, and returns nothing when it is true. `isCustomizationPackage` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts`) is "some base derives this id", so the sentence's "a `.custom` package" is exactly the predicate's set. The refusal message carries the `place` prescription.
- Save: `protocol-save.ts:1390` asks `objectExtensionItemRefusal` (`protocol-object-extension-item.ts`), whose step 8 calls the judge with the write's package binding; a write that names no package is already refused at step 1. Publish: `protocol-history-and-publish.ts:1062`, the same gate. Install: `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3192`, the judge over every delivered package body, answered 422 before anything is written. `os validate`: `validate.ts:895`; `os build`: `compile.ts:948`; both through `findExtensionArrangementRefusals` (`packages/cli/src/utils/extension-arrangement.ts`), which hands the judge each package of the artifact. So every writer that is a package and is not a `.custom` package is refused at each of the five doors. The sentence holds.
- What it no longer claims: a `.custom` package that is not the object's pair. `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_WRITER` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:6828`) says such a package "is not refused at those doors: the registry merge does not apply what it writes here ... and the boot log names it", and the judge agrees. The new sentence says nothing about that writer, and the paragraph's first sentence ("Only the pair's extension may also write ...") stays true of it (the fold serves the object's own pair only). Nothing false is taught about it.
- The rest of the paragraph and the five payment hunks are byte-identical to the head record 7087999230 judged; its judgments stand.

S1: closed — the sentence now names the refused writer by the judge's own predicate; the changeset bullet carries the same wording.

N3 (nit) — read to the letter, "Outside a `.custom` package" also covers a body that names no package at all, and the judge does not judge one ("A body bound to no package is not judged: the rule is about packages"): a single stack with no `manifest.id` passes `os validate` / `os build` with either key written (`extension-arrangement.ts`, the fallback subject; pinned by "a stack naming no package id is not judged"). At save and publish that writer is refused anyway (step 1 of the item gate), and the paragraph's own frame is packages ("An object an installed package ships ...", "the pair", the neighbouring `__c` sentence's "any other package", which has the same boundary over the same predicate). No effect on what the skill teaches an author of a package; accepted as it stands, no change asked.

**skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json** — case 27, `must_contain` now `hotcrm.custom`, `defineObjectExtension`, `extend: 'crm_account'`, `relatedLists`, `hidden: true`, `place:`.

- Under the literal grader (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`: case-sensitive `includes`, nothing normalised), read by eye against the unchanged reference answer: all six tokens occur; `place:` occurs once, in `place: [{ list: 'acme_contract', after: 'crm_opportunity' }]` (the earlier "prescribes `place`:" has a backtick between the word and the colon, so it is not the match, and "replaces" no longer satisfies the token). Neither forbidden string occurs: `name: 'crm_account'` is absent, and "`overrides` declaration" has a backtick, not a colon, after the word. The reference answer passes its own assertions; the dev's 27/27 is consistent.
- `place:` collides with no `must_not_contain` entry of the case (the two forbidden strings are unrelated to it), and a correct answer has no need of either forbidden string.
- The token is taught by the bundle (`SKILL.md` line 359, `place: [{ field: 'tax_id', ... }]`) and is the token case 26 already asserts. It now makes the prompt's second question ("what may `acme_contracts` write instead?") observable: the answer must write a `place` entry. An answer naming `place` only in prose fails, the same property case 26 has; that is the intended strictness, not a correct answer wrongly caught, since the prompt asks what the package writes.
- Case 26 and the rest of the file did not move in the rework.

N1: closed — the token is `place:`, no longer a substring of "replaces".

N2: carried, accepted as it stands — the clause (a list the owner hid by leaving it out stays hidden until the arrangement names it) was offered only if S1's fix left bytes; the file sits on its ceiling (6,710 of 6,710, ratchet green) and the sentence it would extend is not false. It stays with the key description and the docs page; a follow-up card is the seat's choice, none is owed by this PR.

**skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md** — unchanged in the rework; the one index clause for case 27 still matches the case. Holds.

Attempts to break the reworked text that did not land: a `.custom` id that no base derives (`a.custom.custom`, the bare `.custom`) is not a `.custom` package to the predicate and is refused, as the sentence says; a multi-package artifact whose entry has no `manifest.id` is still judged (the id falls back to `name`, then to the positional spelling, neither a `.custom` id); the install door with a `packages[]` manifest judges each delivered body under its own manifest id, not the outer id alone; an answer to case 27 that writes `place:` but keeps the arrangement on the add-on package still fails on `hotcrm.custom`.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
